examples.name: Counter-sample — graded icons flattened to one glyph
paragraphs: A plant-list table with two icon-valued columns — Sun and H₂O. The printed page on the left uses graded symbols: a filled, a half-filled or an empty sun, and one, two or three water droplets. The parse preview on the right renders both columns as a single ☀️ and a single 💧.

That is the failure this rule exists to prevent. The icons were not dropped — they were flattened. A plant needing three droplets and one needing a single droplet come out identical, so the column still looks populated while the information it carried is gone. The columns are the whole point of the table: Sun and H₂O are the two facts a reader consults it for. The expected Markdown reads the empty sun as [sun: none]; the red outlines around the two columns are highlighting added to the figure, not part of the page.

examples.name: Sample — icons standing in for labels
paragraphs: The footer prints a pin, a handset and a globe before the address, the phone number and the website — no words. The pictorial labels become [address], [phone] and [web] beside their values.

snippets.text: **PAGE 1** [address] 7 Merevald Circle NW Suite 400 Harrowgate, BV 20036 [phone] 202-555-0180 [web] halvernwlc.example
